subject: Bug when plotting density plots for groups with one observation

messages.author: 6d1cd0a71e6148df
messages.subject: Bug when plotting density plots for groups with one observation
parts:
Hi!

I believe I've found one or two bugs in the handling of density plots
in ggplot2. The following code gives a very confusing error message:

$ library(ggplot2)
$ library(plyr)
$
$ movies$decade = round_any(movies$year, 10)
$ ggplot(movies[1:60,], aes(x=rating, colour=decade, group=decade)) +
geom_density(fill=NA)
Error in rowSums(vapply(x, is.finite, logical(nrow(x)))) :
'x' must be an array of at least two dimensions
Error in UseMethod("scale_dimension") :
no applicable method for 'scale_dimension' applied to an object of
class "NULL"

I think the reason for the error message is that in rows 1:60, decade
1930 only occurs once:

> table(movies[1:60,]$decade)

1910 1920 1930 1940 1950 1960 1970 1980 1990 2000
2 2 1 9 2 2 4 7 15 16

It is of course not possible to create a density plot based on only
one observation!

If we include row number 61 (where decade=1930), every thing *appears*
to work fine, i.e., a plot is generated. However, this plot does *not*
contain density estimates for the decades with only two observations;
only five density estimates are shown.

So the problem is that 1) with *one* observation, a confusing error
message is displayed, and 2) with more than one but not enough
observations, no error messages is displayed (but plots for these
groups are not drawn).

I think the best solution would be to draw density plots for the
groups with enough observations, and issue a *warning* (not an error)
if at least one group has too few observations.
